overview: Meningitis is the inflammation of the tissues surrounding the brain and spinal cord, can be infectious or non-infectious in origin, and requires urgent medical care. It can be caused by several species of bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites. Meningitis remains a significant global health threat and can be associated with high risk of death and long-term complications.
symptoms: neurological deficits, such as weakness of the limbs
bulging of the soft spot in the head
transmission: mother to child around the time of birth
prevention: avoiding sharing cups, utensils or toothbrushes
complications: speech, language, memory and communication problems
key_facts: 1 in 6 people who get bacterial meningitis die
1 in 5 people who get bacterial meningitis have severe complications
vaccines are the most effective way to deliver long-lasting protection
